mechanics_canada:
HOW CANADIAN ADMISSION ACTUALLY WORKS FOR HIM. (1) Last-two-years math, honestly: SPA 2.56–3.2 with a 2.09 dip averages roughly 2.6–2.8/4.0 (≈73–77%, B-/low B). That is BELOW the B+ (77–80% / 3.3) last-two-years bar used at Carleton, uOttawa, Toronto, McGill, Dalhousie (3.7!), Manitoba (3.5) and Calgary (3.4). His overall 79.53% looks passable, but Canadian committees weight recent years — so most 'brand' programs are paper Reaches. The two levers before Dec 2026–Jan 2027 deadlines: (a) a strong final SDU year (every A in autumn 2026 semester lands on the transcript he submits), (b) IELTS 7.0 — most schools want 6.5–7.0; his English-medium degree does NOT exempt him because Kazakhstan is not on English-primary-country lists (SFU states this explicitly; Carleton/McGill similar). McGill accepts 6.5 and scores must ARRIVE before Jan 15. Book IELTS by autumn 2026. (2) Deadlines cluster Dec 1, 2026 (uOttawa international — earliest) through Jan 15–31, 2027 (Memorial, Calgary, McGill, Dalhousie, SFU, Munk Jan 28) to ~Feb 1 (Quebec schools, BSIA). He applies in his 7th semester with 6 semesters of transcripts. (3) Funding reality at Canadian masters level: professional schools (NPSIA, Munk MGA, MPPGA, GSPIA, MIPP) do NOT fund international masters students — NPSIA says so outright, BSIA expects third-party funding, UBC's awards (5–30k) don't dent a 94k bill. Thesis-based MAs at smaller universities (Memorial, Regina) are where internationals actually get funded, via Graduate/Teaching Assistantships often written into the offer. Vanier is PhD-only; OGS is essentially domestic. So the honest portfolio: Memorial + Regina as funded anchors, UQAM as the grade-fit Realistic (if French reaches B2/C1 — his 12-month project), NPSIA + GSPIA as the two worth-it Reaches, skip Munk/UBC/Dalhousie/Manitoba entirely. (4) Quebec specifics: the famous tuition treaty covers FRENCH and francophone-Belgian citizens only — a Russian citizen gets nothing from it. But UdeM's Bourse d'exemption is automatic for ALL internationals (tiered by grades), and uOttawa cuts internationals in FRENCH-language programs to domestic rates — his 4 semesters of French (last 95/A, ~B1-B2) are 12 focused months from making that real. (5) Immigration: SDS (Student Direct Stream) was DISCONTINUED Nov 8, 2024 — everyone applies through the regular study-permit stream now. Proof of funds: CAD 20,635+ for living (2025 figure, indexed annually) PLUS first-year tuition PLUS travel — for Memorial that's ~CAD 27k to show, for NPSIA ~CAD 42k; family/sponsor GIC or bank statements needed, a real hurdle on his income (a formal sponsor letter or education loan is standard). Russian citizens face longer processing and extra scrutiny — apply from Kazakhstan immediately upon admission (Feb–Apr 2027) for a Sept start; biometrics in Almaty/Astana. (6) Post-study: masters graduates get a 3-year PGWP regardless of field (masters degrees exempt from the field-of-study restriction), and 24 hrs/week off-campus work is allowed during studies (~CAD 1,600–1,900/month at minimum wage — this materially changes his budget math and is a genuine advantage of Canada over most EU options). (7) Excluded from the table after checking: University of Manitoba (requires 3.5 last two years — not met), Université Laval (viable French-taught twin of the UdeM bet — apply alongside UdeM/UQAM if the French route is chosen). Bottom line: Canada is winnable for him only at Memorial/Regina prices or via the Quebec-French route; the Ottawa/Toronto/Vancouver brands are admissible-on-paper at best and unaffordable in fact.

CANADA ADMISSION + VISA MECHANICS FOR TIMOFEY DEMIDOV (Russian citizen, resident in Kazakhstan, SDU IR grad June 2027, Fall 2027 intake)

1. HONEST GPA POSITIONING (read this first)
Canadian grad schools evaluate the LAST TWO YEARS (last 60 credit hours), not the overall average. Timofey's overall 2.83/4.0 (79.53%) is decent-looking, but his last-2-years standing is WEAKER: recent-semester SPAs of 2.56-3.2 with a 2.09 dip average out to roughly 2.7-2.8/4.0 ≈ C+/B-. Most Canadian universities set a hard formal minimum of B / 3.0 in the final two years (Carleton wants B+ for MA admission; UCalgary and UAlberta 3.0/4.0 over last 60 credits; Waterloo 75%). This means: (a) NOTHING in Canada is a true "Safe" for him; (b) his application must lead with the SDU grading context (pass mark 50%, so 79.53% converts better than it looks on a US-style scale — get a WES or IQAS credential evaluation, ~CAD 220, which often converts Kazakh percentages favorably), the A grades in exactly the relevant courses (International Security 96, Russian Politics 92, IR Theories 90, Research Methods 89), and the native-Russian/Central Asia niche that Canadian Eurasia-focused programs actively want post-2022.

2. HOW MASTERS FUNDING ACTUALLY WORKS IN CANADA
- THESIS-BASED MAs (PolSci at Manitoba, Memorial, Calgary MSS thesis, Carleton EURUS) normally fund admitted students via TA-ship + RA-ship + internal scholarship packages, typically CAD 12,000-20,000/yr. This is the ONLY realistic funding route for him — target thesis programs.
- COURSE-BASED PROFESSIONAL PROGRAMS (Toronto Munk MGA, UBC MPPGA, NPSIA's course pattern for internationals, Queen's MPA) give little or no funding to international students. Munk MGA intl tuition is ~CAD 45-50k/yr (~€29-33k) — categorically unaffordable, excluded.
- NPSIA (Carleton) explicitly states it does NOT offer admission-based funding to international MA students (carleton.ca/npsia/ma-admissions-faq/); domestic students get automatic scholarship+TA consideration. In-program awards exist but cannot be counted on.
- BSIA (Waterloo MAGG / Laurier MIPP) awards Balsillie Graduate Fellowships to SELECT incoming students only — competitive, not guaranteed, and his GPA makes a fellowship unlikely.
- ONTARIO GRADUATE SCHOLARSHIP (OGS, CAD 15,000): international students ARE technically eligible but each university has a tiny international quota (often single digits; Waterloo doesn't even let prospective intl students apply), and it requires A- in each of the last two years — he is NOT competitive. Do not budget around OGS.
- QUEBEC TUITION-FEE EXEMPTIONS (differential fee remission): Quebec has student-mobility agreements with ~40 countries (quebec.ca list). The published lists (Concordia, McGill, HEC references) are dominated by francophone states plus China, Mexico, Israel, Morocco, Algeria, Tunisia, Senegal, Brazil etc. NEITHER KAZAKHSTAN NOR RUSSIA appears in any enumerated list found; even where a country is listed, spots are a small quota allocated by the HOME government, not the university. Treat the Quebec exemption route as UNAVAILABLE to him (verify the current ministry PDF before writing Quebec off entirely, but plan without it). His B1-B2 French is also below the level needed for French-taught Quebec programs (Laval HEI, UdeM).
- EXCLUDED BY DESIGN: Lester B. Pearson = undergraduate-only. Vanier CGS = PhD-only. Neither applies.
- CHEAPEST-TUITION ROUTE: Memorial University of Newfoundland has the lowest international graduate tuition in Canada (roughly CAD 4,800-9,700/yr depending on fee plan) plus fellowships — low tuition is itself the funding strategy there. Manitoba (~CAD 11,700/yr) is second-cheapest among relevant programs.

3. STUDY PERMIT — FINANCIAL PROOF (post-2024 rules)
- Cost-of-living requirement was raised again effective Sept 1, 2025: a single applicant OUTSIDE QUEBEC must now show CAD 22,895 (~€14,880) in living funds PLUS full first-year tuition PLUS travel. So for e.g. Manitoba: ~CAD 22,895 + ~CAD 11,700 ≈ CAD 34,600 (~€22,500) demonstrable at application. Quebec tripled its own proof-of-funds figures for 2026 — another reason Quebec is off the table.
- Acceptable proof: bank statements (4-6 months history preferred), scholarship/assistantship award letters (a funded offer letter DIRECTLY reduces the cash he must show — a CAD 15k TA/RA package letter counts), GICs, sponsor letters. Funds in KZT/RUB must be converted at Bank of Canada rates. On a $300-400/month salary he cannot self-fund this: the admission funding package letter is not just nice-to-have, it is what makes the visa possible.
- Russian citizenship: no bar to a Canadian study permit, but expect security screening to add time; apply from Kazakhstan as country of residence (biometrics at VFS in Almaty/Astana).

4. SDS — CONFIRMED DISCONTINUED
The Student Direct Stream was closed effective Nov 8, 2024, 2:00 p.m. EST (IRCC). Kazakhstan was never SDS-eligible anyway. All applications now go through the regular study-permit stream.

5. PROVINCIAL ATTESTATION LETTERS (PAL) AND CAPS
2024-2025: masters students initially exempt, then pulled INTO the PAL requirement in Jan 2025. CHANGED AGAIN: as of JANUARY 1, 2026, master's and doctoral students at public degree-granting institutions are EXEMPT from the PAL requirement (confirmed by SFU, UBC, uOttawa, Waterloo international-office pages). For a Fall 2027 application filed in 2027, he will NOT need a PAL, and the study-permit cap allocations that squeezed college/undergrad numbers do not constrain masters admissions at public universities. Verify no rule reversal in early 2027 — IRCC has changed this rule twice already.

6. PGWP (the payoff)
- Master's graduates get a 3-YEAR PGWP even if the program is only 1 year (minimum 8 months) — confirmed current for 2026.
- Degree graduates (bachelor's/master's/PhD) are EXEMPT from the field-of-study restrictions that hit college diploma grads.
- New PGWP language requirement for university grads: CLB 7 (IELTS ~6.0 in each band) — his planned IELTS 7.0 clears this.
- 3 years of open work rights + a masters is the standard Express Entry PR pathway; his profile (age ~24-25, masters, CLB 9 if IELTS 7.0+, Canadian work experience) would be genuinely competitive for PR later.

7. IELTS NORMS
Canadian IR/PolSci masters typically want IELTS 6.5 overall / 6.0 minimum per band (Carleton, Manitoba, Memorial, Calgary); NPSIA and Munk effectively expect 7.0. His 7.0 target covers everything; even 6.5 keeps most doors open. TOEFL/PTE accepted everywhere; some schools waive the test for English-medium bachelor's degrees, but SDU (Kazakhstan) is rarely on auto-waiver lists — assume the test is required and take IELTS Academic in Almaty by Oct-Nov 2026.

8. TIMELINE FOR FALL 2027 (SEPT 2027) INTAKE
- Aug-Nov 2026: IELTS; WES/IQAS credential evaluation; contact potential thesis supervisors at Manitoba CDSS / Calgary CMSS / Carleton EURUS (Eurasia-security supervisors actively seek Russian-speaking students — a supervisor champion can outweigh GPA).
- Dec 1, 2026 - Feb 1, 2027: applications. Carleton EURUS: apply BEFORE Feb 1 for automatic funding consideration (intl encouraged by Dec 1). NPSIA: mid-January. Manitoba intl deadline for Fall is typically ~Mar 1 but apply by January for funding. Memorial: Feb 15 for September+fellowship.
- Mar-May 2027: offers with funding letters.
- May-Jun 2027: study permit application (regular stream, no PAL needed, no SDS). Published processing ~4-14 weeks by country; Kazakhstan not separately published — budget 8-12 weeks plus possible security-screening delay for a Russian citizen; apply the day the final transcript/offer allows.
- Graduation June 2027 is tight but workable: Canadian universities issue conditional offers on 7-semester transcripts; final degree proof needed before enrolment.

9. BOTTOM-LINE STRATEGY
Only thesis-based programs with package funding + low tuition make Canada affordable on his budget. The two structurally best bets are Carleton EURUS (guaranteed funding for all admitted, perfect niche fit, but B+ bar = reach) and Manitoba MA Political Studies via CDSS or Memorial MA PolSci (cheapest tuition, B bar he is borderline for). NPSIA/BSIA/Munk are prestige names that do not fund internationals at his GPA — apply to at most one as a lottery ticket. Canada overall remains WEAKER than his Germany/OSCE-Academy/Erasmus-Mundus routes on pure affordability: even the cheapest Canadian option needs ~CAD 30-35k (~€20-23k) demonstrable for the visa, most of which must come from an assistantship package he is not guaranteed to win.
